forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 22%. June 2026 Davos restated the familiar split — Amodei ~2027, Hassabis ~50% by 2030, Altman 'within the presidential term' while calling AGI 'not a super useful term'. No new resolution-grade event (no clean lab AGI declaration, no convergence of 3+ leading researchers), so no material move.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: near-term insider predictions of a transformative technology arriving within a fixed ~3.5-year window, where insiders carry optimism incentives. Such forecasts resolve YES well under half the time; base ~15-20%.

factors_up.factor: Lab leadership timelines (Amodei ~2027, Hassabis ~50% by 2030, Altman 2026-2028) sit partly inside the window
Recursive self-improvement / coding-automation signals continue to accelerate capability gains

factors_down.factor: Resolution bar (clean credible declaration or 3+ researchers) remains unmet and definitionally contested
Labs and leaders (notably Altman) increasingly avoid formally using 'AGI', reducing chance of a clean declaration

key_uncertainties: Whether any major lab will formally declare 'AGI' rather than avoiding the term
Whether 3+ leading researchers would publicly converge on 'AGI achieved' before 2030
update_triggers: Revise UP if a credible lab announces AGI or 3+ leading researchers state it is achieved
Revise DOWN if frontier progress visibly plateaus or labs explicitly disavow near-term AGI

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 1pp to 24%. Fresh evidence of structural pressure: McKinsey planning ~10% cuts (3,000-4,000 roles) explicitly tied to AI, Bain/BCG/Deloitte slowing hiring, junior consultant hiring down ~40%, and ~40% productivity gains reported at AI-adopting firms. Still well short of a ≥33% revenue/employment decline, and Accenture revenue is still growing, so the move is small.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: established professional-services sectors experiencing a ≥33% revenue or employment collapse within ~6 years attributable primarily to a single technology. Historically rare; base ~10-15%.

factors_up.factor: Concrete AI-attributed cuts now visible at top firms (McKinsey ~10%, peers slowing hiring) and ~40% junior hiring decline
Documented ~40% productivity gains compress billable hours and headcount needs

factors_down.factor: 33% is a very high bar; current cuts are partial/back-office, and overall sector revenue (e.g. Accenture) still growing
Attribution 'primarily to AI' by 2+ credible analyses is demanding; cycle/macro effects confound

key_uncertainties: Whether headcount cuts translate into a ≥33% revenue decline or are offset by AI-driven new demand
Whether analyses will attribute any decline primarily to AI vs. macro/cyclical factors
update_triggers: Revise UP if sector revenue or employment data show a sustained double-digit decline attributed to AI
Revise DOWN if firms rebuild headcount or revenue grows on AI-enabled new service lines

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 6%. Late-May/June 2026 polling has Reform ~27%, Labour ~19%, Conservatives ~19% — Labour running second/third and well behind Reform, with Starmer's ratings poor. With the GE not due until 2029 there is recovery time, but the current gap keeps the probability low.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: governing party trailing the lead party by ~8pp mid-term, recovering to win most seats at an election up to ~3 years later. Possible but a minority of cases; base ~15-20%, lowered by the unusual multi-party fragmentation.

factors_up.factor: Election not due until 2029 leaves substantial time for poll reversion and incumbency tools
Fragmented right (Reform vs Conservatives) and FPTP can let Labour win most seats on a modest vote share

factors_down.factor: Reform's sustained ~8pp lead over Labour since 2025 and poor PM ratings
Labour third/tied-second in vote share with no clear recovery trend

key_uncertainties: Whether Reform's lead proves durable or is a mid-term protest peak
How vote fragmentation converts to seats under FPTP
update_triggers: Revise UP if Labour regains a polling lead or Reform support fades materially
Revise DOWN if Reform consolidates the lead into the pre-election period

forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2035?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 82%. The longer ~9-year window comfortably encompasses essentially all current lab-leader timelines (Amodei, Hassabis, Altman, Legg). No new information shifts the longer-horizon view; the main risk remains definitional resolution rather than capability.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: expert consensus that a transformative technology arrives within a long (~9-year) window, with rapid current progress. Such longer-horizon insider expectations resolve YES more often than near-term ones; base ~55-65%.

factors_up.factor: Nearly all major lab leaders expect AGI well inside the window
Sustained capability scaling plus automation of AI R&D raises the ceiling over a 9-year horizon

factors_down.factor: Definitional/resolution risk: 'AGI achieved' may stay contested even with strong capabilities
Possible scaling plateau or compute/energy constraints over the decade

key_uncertainties: Whether a recognised resolution event (lab declaration or researcher consensus) occurs even if capabilities are high
Whether progress sustains or hits a multi-year plateau
update_triggers: Revise UP if frontier systems clearly automate most cognitive work and researchers converge on 'AGI'
Revise DOWN if progress plateaus for an extended period

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged down 1pp to 7%. June 2026 assessments are mildly reassuring: the US judges an imminent attack unlikely, analysts say Beijing has 'set aside the option of an invasion for at least the next two years', and economic/demographic headwinds plus PLA leadership purges dampen appetite — even as large blockade-style exercises (e.g. late-2025 'Justice Mission') continue.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: a major power initiating a blockade/invasion of a specific neighbour within a fixed ~3.5-year window despite strong deterrents. Historically low; base ~5-10%.

factors_up.factor: Repeated large-scale PLA blockade/assault rehearsals signal capability and intent build-up
Long-run CCP commitment to 'reunification' and unpredictable cross-strait triggers

factors_down.factor: US and analysts assess near-term action unlikely; leadership reportedly shelving invasion for ~2 years
Chinese economic/demographic headwinds and military leadership purges reduce readiness/appetite

key_uncertainties: Whether a Taiwan political trigger (e.g. independence move) or external shock changes Beijing's calculus
Whether exercises escalate into a sustained >72hr blockade
update_triggers: Revise UP on a sustained blockade, mobilisation, or sharp cross-strait escalation
Revise DOWN on cross-strait de-escalation or credible restraint signals

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged down 1pp to 2%. ONS May 2026 CPI held at 2.8% (core up to 2.6%, services surging, transport at +6.8%). Only ~6 monthly prints remain that could be published before 1 Jan 2027, and inflation would need to drop ~0.8pp+ rapidly against clear upward pressure — very unlikely.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: probability that headline CPI, currently ~0.8pp above target with rising core/services, prints below 2.0% in any of ~6 remaining months. Low; base ~5%.

factors_up.factor: Food inflation decelerating (2.2%, lowest since Dec 2024) and possible energy base effects
Any sharp demand or commodity shock could pull a single month below 2.0%

factors_down.factor: Headline stuck at 2.8% with core rising to 2.6% and services surging
Transport +6.8% (highest since Dec 2022) and limited months left to publish

key_uncertainties: Whether a large one-off downward shock hits before the cut-off
Energy/base-effect path over the remaining months
update_triggers: Revise UP if a monthly print falls toward ~2.2% or core/services ease sharply
Revise DOWN if inflation stays at/above ~2.8%

forecasts.question: Will Spider-Man: Brand New Day gross over $1.5B worldwide by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 1pp to 86%. With the 31 July 2026 release approaching, the film posted the strongest first-day US presales in five years and is tracking for a ~$250M domestic opening (biggest since No Way Home), even without IMAX in the opening frame. Demand signals firmly support clearing $1.5B, leaving ~5 months of runway.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: MCU Spider-Man tentpoles — only No Way Home ($1.92B) cleared $1.5B; Far From Home reached $1.13B. So the bar sits above all but one prior entry; unconditional base ~40-50%, but this title's tracking is exceptional.

factors_up.factor: Record-breaking presales and ~$250M opening tracking imply a very high final gross
Strong franchise multipliers and ~5 months of post-release runway in 2026

factors_down.factor: $1.5B is elite territory only one Spider-Man film has reached
China access, competition (Avengers: Doomsday, Toy Story 5) and IMAX-less opening frame

key_uncertainties: Final domestic multiplier from the record opening
update_triggers: Revise UP on a record opening weekend confirming the tracking
Revise DOWN on a soft opening or weak international rollout

forecasts.question: Will OpenAI and Anthropic have a combined ARR exceeding $70B by 31 December 2026?
forecasts.key_change: Held at 99%. Mid-May 2026 run-rates already sum to roughly $70B+ (Anthropic ~$47B, OpenAI ~$25B), both still growing fast. Even applying OpenAI's disputed ~$8B haircut to Anthropic's figure, continued growth through Q4 makes >$70B by year-end near-certain.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: a near-term financial threshold already essentially met by current run-rates of rapidly growing firms. Base ~95%+.

factors_up.factor: Combined run-rate already at/above the threshold in mid-2026 with steep growth
Both firms scaling enterprise/API revenue; OpenAI filed S-1 (financial scrutiny rising)

factors_down.factor: Definitional disputes over ARR (gross vs net) could shave reported figures
Tail risk of a sharp demand/funding shock before year-end

key_uncertainties: Which ARR definition credible reporting uses for each company at Q4 2026
Any abrupt macro or sector shock late in the year
update_triggers: Revise DOWN only on a severe revenue collapse or a much stricter ARR redefinition
Revise UP is moot at this level

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Nudged up 1pp to 40%. OBR (March 2026) pegs medium-term potential growth at ~1.5% with real GDP 'steady at around 1.5%' as TFP rises to 0.8% by 2030 — placing the decade average right on the threshold. Downside productivity risk is explicitly flagged, but AI-driven upside optionality keeps this a sub-coin-flip rather than lower.
forecasts.base_rate: Reference class: realised UK decade-average real GDP growth exceeding ~1.5%. The 2010s averaged ~1.9% but the trend has slowed; recent potential estimates cluster ~1.5%, making 'exceeds' roughly a coin flip.

factors_up.factor: OBR central potential growth ~1.5% with TFP projected to rise to 0.8% by 2030
AI/automation could lift productivity above the central trajectory over a full decade

factors_down.factor: Explicit OBR downside: if productivity recovery fails, output ~3.2% lower by end-decade
Ageing population and lower net migration cut labour-supply growth toward ~0.5%

key_uncertainties: Whether the projected productivity/TFP recovery actually materialises
Net migration and labour-supply path through the 2030s
update_triggers: Revise UP on sustained productivity acceleration or upgraded potential-growth estimates
Revise DOWN if productivity continues to track its weak recent trend
